title: Great Mosque of Djenné
summary: The Great Mosque of Djenné in Mali is a Sudano-Sahelian mud-brick mosque, rebuilt in 1906-1907 under French colonial administration on the site of an older mosque that tradition dates to 1280. Its walls are replastered with mud every year. A restoration financed by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture began in 2009.

uncertainty.note: The present building dates to 1906-1907 (Zamani Project) or 1907 (UNESCO, Harvard). End is the present. Zamani gives 1280 for the first mosque on the site, not for the standing building.

as_recorded.value: the current mosque was built between 1906 and 1907

reviewer_note: Shape block (rectangular mass with towers; no dome). Least sure of the dimensions: Zamani Project (University of Cape Town) lists 85 x 65 m and an 18 m central minaret, while other popular accounts (not opened) give a 75 x 75 m platform and about 16 m; the Zamani figures are the only university or museum measurements found. The standing mosque is the 1906-07 rebuilding; the 1280 first mosque is not modelled.
